title: About Erazahan
description: About Erazahan, its historical source, and the principles used to preserve traditional dream interpretations.
body_markdown:
Erazahan is a project dedicated to traditional dream interpretations preserved in an old printed dream dictionary that has remained in our family.

The main historical source behind the project is **«Համամարդկային Երազահան»**, published in **1969**. The copy on which the website is based was passed down to me through my grandmother and remained in our family for many years.

Around fifteen years ago, I began bringing the book's material online. In the earliest version of the website, pages from the book were published as images. Over time, the material was gradually converted into text so that individual interpretations could be easier to find and read.

## The book's sources

The 1969 edition states that its compilers drew on several earlier dream dictionaries translated from older source texts and already out of circulation at the time. Among the works it names are:

- **«Բախտացոյց Երազահան»**, published in Constantinople;
- **«Երազահան եւ Վիճակարան»**, published in Jerusalem;
- **«Զավեշտագիրք Երազահան»**, published in America;
- **«Պատկերազարդ Երազահան»** by Cagliostro, published in Constantinople;
- **«Տիեզերական Երազահան»**, published in Egypt.

The book also states that it combines Eastern, European, and Greek traditions of dream study and interpretation. In its own introduction, the edition describes itself as one of the most extensive dream dictionaries published up to that time and says that it contains interpretations for approximately **4,000 dreams and symbols**.

## What we preserve

The central principle of Erazahan is not to invent new meanings in place of those found in the historical source.

We aim to preserve the traditional meaning of each interpretation as closely as possible. The wording may be edited or accompanied by explanation so that it is understandable to a modern reader.

The Russian and English editions of the site follow the same principle: when wording is translated or adapted, the meaning of the original interpretation should remain intact.

## A note for readers

The dream interpretations on this site reflect traditional beliefs, folklore, and historical approaches to symbolism.

They are provided for cultural, informational, and personal reflection and should not be treated as guaranteed predictions, medical advice, or psychological advice.
